carbon.$description: Carbon — Primary text, headings, nav links — near-black with the faintest cool tint gives type a deliberate, engineered weight without pure-black harshness

paper-white.$description: Paper White — Page canvas, card surfaces, button fills — the base layer everything sits on

linen.$description: Linen — Subtle background sections, table rows, secondary surfaces — separates content bands from pure white without introducing a visible gray

mist.$description: Mist — Primary page canvas and white card surfaces. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

fog.$description: Fog — Table gridlines, hairline borders, divider lines — the structural 1px that defines table cells and card edges

ash.$description: Ash — Muted body text, placeholder text, inactive nav items — secondary information that recedes

graphite.$description: Graphite — Secondary text, button text on light fills, captions — readable but clearly subordinate to Carbon

lavender.$description: Lavender — Violet action color for filled buttons, selected navigation states, and focused conversion moments.

iris.$description: Iris — Register button and gradient endpoint — a slightly deeper lavender for secondary action emphasis

mint.$description: Mint — Green text accent for links, tags, and emphasized short phrases. Use as a supporting accent, not as a status color

mint-wash.$description: Mint Wash — Soft section background, alternate surface, and quiet card fill. Use as a supporting accent, not as a status color

amber.$description: Amber — Yellow text accent for links, tags, and emphasized short phrases

sky.$description: Sky — Violet text accent for links, tags, and emphasized short phrases.

magenta.$description: Magenta — Visitor profiles category, icon accents — vivid pink that earns its place by mapping to one specific feature domain

ember.$description: Ember — Chart fill accents, decorative illustration — warm orange that breaks the cool palette inside data visualizations

openrunde.$description: Single typeface across all UI — geometric humanist sans with tight apertures and slightly compressed proportions. Display headlines at 60px/600 with -3px tracking feel engineered; body at 16px/400 with -0.32px tracking reads crisp without feeling clinical.
